subject: Polaris Labs pilot: trial readiness, roles, and decision gates
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Malik <sana@polaris.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@polaris.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Polaris Labs pilot — scope, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Sana,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed path to get the pilot ready:

Pain points we heard
- Search relevancy drops for new product catalogs (especially category mapping)
- High per-query latency for large result sets during peak hours
- Manual tagging and classification adds 2-3 FTEs to weekly QA

Goals for the pilot
- Reduce mean query latency to < 120ms for catalog search
- Improve top-5 relevance metric by >= 12% on your labeled sample
- Automate tagging workflow to remove manual steps for 75% of items

Proposed pilot attributes
- Duration: 6 weeks (2-week onboarding, 4-week measurement)
- Environment: Dedicated trial in us-west (private VPC optional)
- Data: sample catalog (up to 10M SKUs index), subset will be redacted
- Success criteria: metric thresholds above + mutual sign-off on evaluation set

Stakeholders & decision process
- Polaris product: Sana Malik (Evaluation lead)
- Polaris procurement: Procurement Team (contract & PO)
- Redwood: Irene Choi (AE), Ben Carter (Solutions Eng), Aditya Rao (CS)
- Decision gate: post-measurement executive review (Polaris product + procurement)

Immediate asks
1) Can you confirm procurement contact and PO timeline?
2) Will you share the sample catalog CSV by next Tues (2028-09-19)?
3) Are there security exceptions we should expect (SAML, IP allowlist)?

I've attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (RWD-Polaris-MAP-v1.pdf) and a high-level cost estimate. If that looks right I'll convert the MAP to a shared Google doc so we can assign owners and dates.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: RWD-Polaris-MAP-v1.pdf, RWD-cost-estimate-PL-7843.xlsx

From: Sana Malik <sana@polaris.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@polaris.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Polaris Labs pilot — scope, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Irene,

Appreciate the clear summary. A few notes from the Polaris side after an internal sync:

Procurement and timeline
- Procurement confirms we will need a 60-day review, but can issue a PO faster if the SOW is under our template and security review is standard
- Point of contact for procurement is procurement@polaris.ai (copied)

Data and security
- We will share a sampled catalog CSV by 2028-09-19; it will be a redacted export (no PII)
- Attached is our security questionnaire in case Redwood wants to pre-fill sections (Polaris_Security_Questionnaire.pdf)
- We prefer SAML SSO for the console and IP allowlist for API access

Stakeholders and decision gates
- Product lead: Sana Malik (evaluation + exec review)
- Engineering reviewer: Marco Ruiz (marco.ruiz@polaris.ai) — expect a technical call next week
- Procurement: procurement@polaris.ai will lead contracting

Commercial
- We need a high level estimate to present to the procurement committee; please confirm any hosted vs dedicated cost delta

Next steps
- Please send the SOW and a version of the MAP that includes specific dates and owner assignments. If you can get that to us by Wednesday (2028-09-20) we will try to accelerate PO processing.

Thanks,

Sana Malik
Head of Product | Polaris Labs
sana@polaris.ai

Attachments: Polaris_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Malik <sana@polaris.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@polaris.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Polaris MAP and SOW draft attached — proposed owners and dates

Sana — thanks, noted. Per your ask we converted the MAP into action items with owners and provisional dates. Below is the mutual action plan summary; the full PDF and editable Google doc are attached and linked. Please review and confirm or suggest edits.

Mutual Action Plan (summary)
1) Kickoff and access (Onboarding)
   Owner: Ben Carter (Redwood) / Marco Ruiz (Polaris eng)
   Target date: 2028-09-25
   Deliverables: Access to dedicated trial endpoint, SSO config, sample data ingest checklist

2) Baseline and instrumentation
   Owner: Aditya Rao (Redwood CS) / Sana Malik (Polaris product)
   Target date: 2028-10-02
   Deliverables: Baseline metrics, evaluation dataset, dashboard access

3) Iteration and tuning (measurement window)
   Owner: Ben Carter (Redwood) / Polaris eng (Marco Ruiz)
   Target date: 2028-10-30
   Deliverables: Weekly checkpoints, relevance improvements, latency reports

4) Executive review & decision gate
   Owner: Sana Malik (Polaris) / Irene Choi (Redwood)
   Target date: 2028-11-06
   Decision: Proceed to purchase committed capacity OR extend trial for an additional 4 weeks

Dependencies and notes
- Procurement approval required before any committed capacity is provisioned
- Security questionnaire review may add ~10 business days if there are open items
- Data handling: we'll implement field-level redaction for any sensitive attributes during the ingest

Requested confirmations
- Can procurement share the expected PO date range once they review the SOW?
- Can Marco join a technical kickoff on 2028-09-26 or 2028-09-27?

Attachments included: RWD-Polaris-MAP-v1.pdf (editable), RWD-cost-estimate-PL-7843.xlsx

If this looks correct I will convert the MAP to a shared Google doc and add checkboxes for each owner so we can mark progress.

Best,

Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 18 Sep 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Polaris MAP and SOW draft — pricing confirmation

Irene / Aditya,

Quick internal note on commercials before we send the SOW: the estimate in the workbook assumes a dedicated trial with a small committed discount (10%). If Polaris prefers hosted burst capacity instead of dedicated VPC we can drop the cost by approximately 22% but latency SLOs will be best-effort.

Recommendation: keep the MAP as written (dedicated trial) and offer a hosted fallback in the SOW as an option with clear performance caveats. That gives Polaris a safe path to start quickly while leaving the dedicated option for committed capacity after the executive review.

I can attach a brief tradeoff blurb to the SOW.

Ben

Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
